Καὶ ἐπεὶ τοῦ βίου τὰ πράγματα ματαιότης, ποντοπορούντων ἀεὶ, καὶ μηδενὸς τῶν
ἀνθρώπων προάγοντος εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, οὐ δυνατὸν νοηθῆναι τὰς τρίβους αὐτῶν.
Τοιγαροῦν τῶν ἐνδόξων τῆς γῆς βασιλέων ἢ καὶ ἀρχόντων ἀλλότριον θεοσεβείας
ἔργον οὐδὲν καταλείπεται μετὰ τελευτήν. Ἐσβέσθη γὰρ αὐτῶν ἡ δόξα. Οὐκ
ἐπιγινώσκονται δὲ, φησὶν, οὐδὲ ὁδοὶ ἀνδρὸς ἐν νεότητι, ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις
πεπυρωμένου διὰ τὸ ἄστατον τῶν τρόπων· καὶ τῆς μοιχαλίδος, ὁμοίως διὰ τὸ
ἀναίσχυντον. Ἢ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἡ τῶν ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησία, ἥτις μετὰ τὸ ἀπολούσασθαι διὰ
τοῦ βαπτίσματος οὐδέν φησιν ἄτοπον πεπραχέναι. Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν
νεότητι, ἐπεὶ, τελειωθεὶς ἐν ὀλίγῳ, ἐπλήρωσε χρόνους μακρούς. Τοιαύτη καὶ πᾶσα
γυνὴ μοιχαλὶς, ἢ ἀλλοτριώσασα ἑαυτὴν τοῦ νυμφίου, καὶ ψυχὴ καταλιποῦσα τὸν
ἄνδρα, καὶ ὀπίσω τῶν ἐραστῶν πορευομένη. Καὶ ἐκστρατεύει ἀφ' ἑνὸς κελεύσμα
pass_a_gloss: …travels the deep, and does this through everything, thrown into unrest by the winds set against it. And because the affairs of life are vanity — of people always traveling the deep, and of no human being advancing into life everlasting — it is not possible for their paths to be grasped. For that reason, of the glorious kings of the earth or also of rulers, no work foreign to reverence for God is left behind after the end; for their glory has been quenched. And they are not recognized either, he says, nor the roads of a man in youth, fired by desires because of the unsettled state of habits; and of the adulterous woman likewise because of the shamelessness. Or this is the Church of the nations, which after being washed clean through the baptism says she has practiced nothing out of place. But the righteous one is not in youth, since, having been perfected in a little, he filled out long times. Such also is every adulterous woman, or a soul that alienated herself from the bridegroom and left the husband and went behind the lovers. And she campaigns out from one single order, in good array. As well-ordered the locust also is praised, persuaded by the order of the Word of God. Such a sort is the Church, because of being despised from the side of humans, compared to a locust with respect to living upon earth; yet because of being gathered with Jesus
pass_b_english: …goes through the sea, and does so always, thrown off balance by opposing winds. And since life’s affairs are vanity—people always at sea, and no one advancing into eternal life—their paths cannot be grasped. So of the famous kings of the earth, or rulers too, no work foreign to piety is left after death; their glory has gone out.

He also says the ways of a man in youth are not recognized, inflamed by desires because manners are unstable; and of the adulteress likewise, because of shamelessness. Or this is the Church of the nations, which after washing through baptism says she has done nothing out of place. The righteous one is not “in youth,” since, perfected in a little, he filled long times. Such also is every adulterous woman—or a soul that alienated herself from the bridegroom, left her husband, and went after lovers.

“And she marches out from one command in good order.” The locust too is praised as orderly, obeying the command of God’s Word. Such is the Church: despised by people and compared to a locust as to living on the earth; yet because she gathers with Jesus
